decisions.title: Phase 1/2 business-rule source authority
decisions.decision_statement: Identify and authorize the consolidated Phase 1/2 business-rule source, or formally define the audit boundary without it.
evidence_required: Authoritative artifact locator or explicit owner declaration of unavailability
SHA-256 and provenance if an artifact is supplied

recommendation.rationale: Binding the original corpus gives the strongest completeness and supersession evidence, but the artifact has not been located.

options.label: Bind the original authoritative corpus
options.outcome: Register the exact Phase 1/2 artifact by locator, hash, provenance and supersession mapping.

impacts.domain: May reveal omitted or superseded invariants.
impacts.application: May alter later design priorities only after comparison.
impacts.api: No direct change; future API scope must trace to approved rules.
impacts.security: Read-only evidence; no secret or runtime data.

options.label: Formally close the corpus as unavailable
options.outcome: Declare repository evidence from later canonical phases as the bounded authority for 12.17.

impacts.product: Allows progress with an explicit completeness limitation.

options.label: Create a provisional reconstruction
options.outcome: Infer a non-authoritative Phase 1/2 index from later ADRs and handoffs, clearly labelled reconstructed.

impacts.product: Improves navigation but not original-source completeness.
impacts.tests: Test provenance labels and non-authoritative status.

options.label: Keep the authority gap open
options.outcome: Do not start dependent rationalization of source authority.

decisions.title: Legacy-reuse trace disposition
decisions.decision_statement: Select the canonical trace location and disposition the Phase 7 adaptation already cited by Phase 12.15.

recommendation.rationale: A retrospective, evidence-bound trace satisfies the declared location without rewriting or retroactively reapproving history.

options.label: Create a retrospective canonical trace
options.outcome: Create a docs/legacy-review record linked to Phase 12.15 evidence and explicitly state that it records, not reauthorizes, the prior adaptation.

impacts.security: Trace excludes runtime data and secrets.

options.label: Supersede the mandated trace location
options.outcome: Declare the Phase 12.15 handoff itself canonical and update the governance policy in a later authorized lot.

impacts.product: Uses existing evidence but changes governance convention.

options.label: Freeze as a documented non-conformance
options.outcome: Preserve the Phase 7 reuse as a closed baseline exception and do not attempt retrospective conformity.

impacts.tests: Test that the exception cannot authorize new reuse.

options.label: Retain the trace gap
options.outcome: Keep EX-01 in EVIDENCE_GAP state.

impacts.security: Future reuse remains prohibited by default.

decisions.title: Application ownership for CAP-R02, CAP-A01 and CAP-A02
decisions.decision_statement: Choose the ownership model and delivery order for read-production, deterministic validation and promotion.

recommendation.rationale: Three explicit bounded Application use cases preserve responsibility separation and prevent route metadata from becoming business authority.

options.label: Three bounded Application owners
options.outcome: Deliver CAP-R02, then CAP-A01, then CAP-A02 as separate query/command owners with explicit handoffs.

impacts.product: Completes the minimum lifecycle authority chain incrementally.
impacts.domain: Adds bounded concepts only where rules require them.
impacts.sqlite: Ports map later; no direct SQL ownership.
impacts.migration: Only if approved models require it later.
impacts.tests: Use-case, negative authority and transition tests.

options.label: One lifecycle Application module
options.outcome: Group the three use cases under one lifecycle module while retaining separate commands and authorities.

impacts.product: Faster shared delivery but larger coupling surface.
impacts.domain: Requires a coherent lifecycle aggregate boundary.
impacts.api: One facade can expose several operations later.
impacts.sqlite: One mapping layer can concentrate literals.
impacts.security: Authority separation must be enforced internally.

options.label: Keep capabilities projected only
options.outcome: Formally declare CAP-R02/A01/A02 out of the current delivery scope and prevent registry metadata from implying implementation.

impacts.sqlite: Existing adapter paths remain technical only.

options.label: Keep routes non-authoritative
options.outcome: No capability implementation or exposure may proceed.

decisions.title: First /api/v2 delivery scope
decisions.decision_statement: Choose the first HTTP scope and confirm that transport delegates to an authoritative Application use case.
decisions.dependency_note: OPTION_A can use the already-concrete Resource Library; OPTIONS B/C involving non-resource capabilities require OD-03.

recommendation.rationale: A read-only Resource Library slice is the only HTTP candidate with an existing concrete Application owner.

options.label: Resource READ-15 only
options.outcome: Design one read-only /api/v2 resource lookup that maps strictly to GetResourceQuery.

impacts.api: One bounded read endpoint and error mapping.
impacts.tests: Contract, validation, not-found and no-direct-store tests.

options.label: Lifecycle API after OD-03
options.outcome: Expose read-production, validation and promotion only after their separate Application owners are approved and implemented.

options.label: No HTTP API in current scope
options.outcome: Keep Application inbounds only and deprecate the current /api/v2 projection as a delivery promise.

impacts.tests: Architecture tests assert absence of direct transport access.

options.label: Keep /api/v2 blocked
options.outcome: Do not design or implement endpoints.

decisions.title: External SQLite schema evidence
decisions.decision_statement: Choose whether and how to bind the exact external canonical SQLite seed for read-only structural verification.
evidence_required: Exact seed locator supplied outside Git
Read-only schema inventory for 98 tables, 20 indexes, 7 triggers and 2 views

recommendation.rationale: Hash-bound read-only introspection closes structural evidence without transferring or versioning the database.

options.label: Authorize hash-bound read-only introspection
options.outcome: Inspect only schema metadata from the exact external seed and emit a minimized manifest.

impacts.domain: Reveals constraints that models must represent.
impacts.sqlite: Read-only metadata inspection of exact seed.
impacts.migration: Validates additive migration preconditions without applying them.
impacts.tests: Schema contract tests can be specified.
impacts.security: No row data, copy, mutation or Git inclusion.

options.label: Accept the external evidence gap
options.outcome: Keep all nine mappings marked EXTERNAL_SCHEMA_EVIDENCE_REQUIRED and prohibit structural equivalence claims.

impacts.application: Port design may proceed with caveats.

options.label: Provide a signed schema-only export
options.outcome: Owner supplies a minimized DDL/metadata artifact with provenance instead of granting direct seed access.

impacts.product: Can close many structural checks if complete.
impacts.security: Must exclude rows, paths, secrets and personal data.

options.label: Keep all schema checks blocked
options.outcome: No alignment or equivalence decision may rely on the external schema.

decisions.title: Ownership of SQLite literal/default families
decisions.decision_statement: Assign business or technical ownership to the ten status/type/title/actor/default families before alignment.

recommendation.rationale: Per-bounded-context vocabulary with explicit adapter translation preserves business ownership and avoids shared-kernel specialization.

options.label: Bounded-context vocabulary ownership
options.outcome: Assign each family to its Domain/Application context and map explicitly in adapters.

impacts.api: Maps owned values without leaking DB literals.
impacts.migration: Only if stored vocabulary must change.

options.label: Application-level canonical vocabulary
options.outcome: Define transport-neutral Application contracts shared by several bounded contexts, with Domain translation where needed.

impacts.security: Authority rules must remain separate from statuses.

options.label: Declare literals technical-only
options.outcome: Freeze current literals as adapter implementation details and prohibit treating them as business states.

impacts.product: Avoids premature domain modelling but leaves lifecycle capability incomplete.
impacts.application: Must not expose literals as decisions.

options.label: Preserve adapter literals unchanged
options.outcome: No new code may rely on them as canonical business vocabulary.

decisions.title: READ-15 version_ref/include scope
decisions.decision_statement: Decide whether the deferred options are deprecated, retained as an explicit future contract, or implemented later.
decisions.external_schema_evidence_note: Required for OPTION_C implementation because version/include storage semantics cannot be inferred from adapter queries.

recommendation.rationale: Removing the deferred options from the active promise keeps the delivered READ-15 contract honest; future needs can open a versioned use case.

options.label: Deprecate from active READ-15 scope
options.outcome: Record version_ref/include as non-goals of the current use case and require a new contract for future support.

impacts.tests: Contract rejects or omits deprecated options.

options.label: Retain an explicitly deferred contract
options.outcome: Keep the names as future reserved options with mandatory fail-closed rejection today.

impacts.api: May reserve names but must reject them.
impacts.tests: Negative tests for every reserved option.

options.label: Approve future implementation
options.outcome: Define version and include semantics in a separate authorized slice after schema evidence and consumer requirements.

impacts.application: New or expanded use case contract.
impacts.tests: Version selection, include allowlist and compatibility tests.
impacts.security: Include must be strictly allowlisted and bounded.

options.label: Keep current ambiguity bounded
options.outcome: Do not claim support and do not alter the current contract.

decisions.title: Durable calibration governance boundary
decisions.decision_statement: Separate durable calibration rules from V4/V5.x historical controls and define the process for any future release threshold.
evidence_required: Phase 12.16 immutable history and final configuration

recommendation.rationale: General blind/provider-neutral/lineage rules remain useful while consumed authorizations and incident-specific mechanics belong to immutable history.

options.label: Generalize policy and archive version-specific controls
options.outcome: Keep blind scoring, strong-only semantics, exact authorization and certified lineage; archive V4/V5.x mechanics as non-runtime history; threshold remains NONE.

impacts.product: Clarifies that calibration is evidence, not release authority.
impacts.security: Exact authorization and minimized transfer remain fail-closed.

options.label: Keep all V4/V5.x controls canonical
options.outcome: Retain every version-specific live, carry-forward and output-bound rule as active canonical policy.

impacts.product: Maximum forensic continuity but high policy complexity.
impacts.tests: All historical contract variants remain maintained.
impacts.security: Strong guards retained, larger policy surface.

options.label: Deprecate live calibration capability
options.outcome: Preserve all evidence read-only but remove live provider execution from future supported scope; threshold remains NONE.

options.label: Preserve current closure unchanged
options.outcome: Live authorization remains consumed/false, threshold NONE and runtime route unchanged.
